Different types of respiratory substrate can have different energy values and therefore release different quantities of energy when they are respired.

Complete Table 1.1 to show the energy value of each of the three main types of respiratory substrate.

parts.stem:
Determining the respiratory quotient (RQ) of an organism can be used to indicate the main type of respiratory substrate that is being metabolised in respiration. This is because the different types of respiratory substrate have different RQ values. Table 1.2 shows typical RQ values for carbohydrate, lipid and protein.

{{figure:reviewed_table_2.png}}

parts.stem:
Organic acids such as malic acid can also act as respiratory substrates. When respired aerobically, their RQ values may be different to the RQ values of the main respiratory substrates.

Fig. 1.1 shows the formula that is used to calculate RQ values.

{{figure:figure-1-1-full-v2.png}}

When malic acid is respired aerobically, the equation is:

C₄H₆O₅ + .......... O₂ → 4CO₂ + 3H₂O + energy

parts.stem:
The deer mouse, *Peromyscus maniculatus*, lives in forests in North America.

Fig. 1.2 shows a deer mouse.

{{figure:figure-1-2.png}}

The deer mouse is active throughout the year and is much more active during the night than during the day.

At certain times of the year, deer mice spend a number of hours during the day in a physiologically controlled state of inactivity (not active), known as torpor. During this time there is a decrease in metabolic rate.

Fig. 1.3 is a graph showing the RQ of a deer mouse from 6:00 to 22:00 on a day that included time in torpor.

{{figure:figure-1-3.png}}
